title: Austin's Future: Zoning & City Improvements
summary:
*   After a significant public hearing with protests from local churches and residents, the city rejected a proposal to rezone residential properties on 14th Street for general commercial use, though temporary state office rental was permitted.
*   The city officially closed its World War II Servicemen's Information Center at the Driskill Hotel and named a new facility the "Pan-Am Recreation Center."
*   Voters approved bonds for critical city upgrades, including funding for hospital improvements, new schools, street enhancements, and a sanitary sewerage system.
*   However, proposed bonds for other projects like an auditorium, airport hangars, electric plant, fire stations, and a police building failed to receive the necessary two-thirds majority vote for approval.

Pursuant to published notice thereof, the public hearing on the proposal of the City
Council to amend the Zoning Ordinance in the following particulars, to-wit: To amend the
USE designation of the following described property so as to change the same from "B"
Residence District, Third Height and Area District to "C" Commercial District, Third
Height and Area District, to-wit: Original Lots 1, 2, 3, 10, 11 and 12, Block 172,
Original Lots 1, 2, 3, 10, 11 and 12, Block 173, City of Austin, located on the north side
of 14th Street, between Colorado and Brazos Streets, City of Austin, Travis *County,
Texas.
The following citizens appeared to protest this change, Rev. Roesner, Pastor of St.
Martin's Luthern Church, Mr. Betts, a member of the Luthern Church Board of Stewards, Rev.
Walter Kerr, pastor of the Central Methodist Church, Mr. D. C. Carlson, a member of the
Central Methodist Church, Mr. H. J. H. Melin, owner of property located at 1409 Congress
Avenue, and a member of the Luthern Church, and representatives of the First Church of
Christ Scientist.
The following citizens appeared to appeal for this change: Mrs. Wayne Huff, Mrs. S. W.
Johnson, and Mrs. Ethel Hartman.
After a lenghty discussion, pro and con, Councilman Wolf moved that the recommendation of
the Zoning Board of Adjustment to grant this change be NOT sustained, but that Mrs. S. W.
Johnson and Mrs. Ethel Hartman, two of the applicants, be referred to the Zoning Board of
Adjustment for an appeal for a tempo- rary use permit which would permit them to rent
their property to the State of Texas for office space. Upon the following vote, the motion
prevailed: Ayes:
Noes:

The following is a copy of a resolution which was passed by the Board of Adjustment at a

Dye, Roy W. Frazier and R. T. Spaw requesting changes in the Use Designation of the
following properties: a. Lots Nos. 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, and 15, Block 2 of the Pecan

C.
312.9 feet by 90 feet deep lying on the West side of Jessie Street, from "A" Residence
District and First Height and Area District to "C" Commercial District and Second Height
and Area District.
WHEREAS, the Board of Adjustment at a meeting on April 30, 1946 carefully considered this
application; and WHEREAS, the Zoning Maps of the City of Austin disclose the fact that the
block containing the lots of Mr. C. E. Dye now has the frontage on Barton Springs Road
zoned as a "C" Commercial District and the block east across Josephine Street is now a
"C-1" Commercial District and the property north across Butler Road fronting thereon is
now a "0-1" Commercial District; and WHEREAS, the property of Mr. R. T. Spaw fronts on
Jessie Street to the west of the block referred to in the preceding paragraph and Lot No.
14 of Mr. Roy W. Frazier lies in the same block with Mr. C. E. Dye's property; and
WHEREAS, should the Use Classification of the property of Mr. R. T.

Spaw be changed as requested, then all of the property of Mr. C. E. Dye and Mr. Roy W.
Frazier would be surrounded by commercial property, and, conversely, should Mr. Dye's
property be changed, then Mr. Spaw's residence property would front on commercial
property; and WHEREAS, an examination of the property in question and the surrounding
neighborhood indicates a continued commercial development along Barton Springs Road and
Lamar Boulevard and the position of this property in the present pattern of zoning would
indicate that the trend of development and the present zoning classification surrounding
it render it less desirable for resi- dential purposes and has an adverse effect on its
character and potential usefulness; and WHEREAS, the Board deemed under these conditions
and circumstances all of this property should be changed rather than one portion or the
other so that all will be treated alike and its use fit into the general scheme of zoning
in this particular area; therefore BE IT RESOLVED BY THE BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT: THAT, the
above changes in the Use Designation of these properties be recommended to the City
Council.
/s/
Respectfully submitted,
BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT
by H. F. Kuehne, Chairman
